Marine Cody Alford on Getting Shot in the Head on 1st Day of Battle of Fallujah (Part 1)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join
--------
Retired Marine Raider and Scout Sniper Cody Alford sits down with VladTV to recount his path from Texas teen inspired by Tom Berenger’s *Sniper* to an 18-year-old Marine deployed to Iraq after 9/11. Alford describes arriving through Kuwait, staging at Bahari near one of Saddam Hussein’s former palace sites, and being attached to Echo Company during the Battle of Fallujah—one of the Iraq War’s most intense urban fights. He breaks down the role of Marine snipers, the presence of foreign fighters, and how units like the 101st Airborne, Delta Force, and 2/1 Marines operated in the chaos. Alford also details the moment he was shot in the helmet on his first day inside Fallujah, the concussion and out-of-body experience that followed, and how the battle quickly proved far different from training at Camp Pendleton.

Charleston White sits down with VladTV as DJ Vlad breaks down his fallout with N.O.R.E., from missed interview plans in Miami and Los Angeles to public shots exchanged on DJ Akademiks and Hot 97. Vlad details why he felt strung along by the Drink Champs host, compares the situation to more direct dealings with Andrew Schulz, Charlamagne Tha God, DeRay Davis and Mike Epps, and explains how business relationships can end without personal disrespect.

Charleston weighs in with his blunt perspective, calling N.O.R.E.’s alleged behind-the-scenes behavior cowardly and arguing that honesty would have avoided the drama. The conversation also touches on N.O.R.E.’s “culture vulture” criticism, Saigon’s attempt to mediate, and the timing of a sexual assault lawsuit filed by N.O.R.E.’s former partner tied to allegations from 1997. Vlad says he had no involvement and reflects on how public conflict can bring unwanted attention.

Part 1: https://youtu.be/U21AbA_cZII
--------
Former Delta Force operator Dale Comstock sits down with Vlad to discuss life after retiring from the military in 2001 at age 38 and spending the next decade as a paramilitary contractor in Afghanistan, Iran, and other conflict zones. Comstock details the dangers of operating with small teams, recruiting and leading indigenous fighters, Taliban infiltration, ambush risks, and the loss of fellow Delta operators during the Global War on Terrorism. He also explains how political restrictions around detentions and interrogations changed the mission on the ground, arguing that bureaucracy put American lives at risk.

Reflecting on war, Comstock agrees with Elon Musk’s widely shared view that wars are often driven by older leaders sending young men to kill one another. He offers a critical but personal perspective on the military, politicians, civilians, and the realities faced by soldiers and contractors in modern warfare.

Charleston White sits down with Vlad for a raw discussion about prison culture, racial dynamics, and sexual violence behind bars. Reacting to Ramon “Mundo” Mendoza’s accounts from Mexican Mafia life, White recalls hearing older inmates say, “in every white boy, there’s a little white girl waiting to come out,” while describing how white inmates were targeted in Texas, Alabama, and other Southern prisons. The conversation also examines how attitudes toward prison assault shifted by the late ’80s and ’90s, plus differences on the East Coast, Washington, D.C., and in facilities seen on MSNBC’s *Lockup*. Vlad and White revisit *American Me*, Edward James Olmos, the controversial Mexican Mafia rape scene, and Mendoza’s claims about Joe Morgan, his brother Angel, Kern County, and the Black Guerrilla Family. A stark look at prison gangs, survival, trauma, and the consequences of gang loyalty.

--------
Nicholas Irving sits down with Shawn Prez for a candid conversation about combat memory, civilian life, and the survival mindset that never fully turns off. Irving explains why he fears losing the violent edge that helped keep him alive, even as he lives a quiet life with his wife and child, writes books, and avoids the spotlight. The discussion touches on Special Forces veterans, Robert O’Neill, “alpha male” culture, Andrew Tate, and the difference between confidence and lived experience. Irving also compares his constant scanning of rooms, exits, and threats to the Jason Bourne mindset, describing how he plans for danger in restaurants, at home, and in everyday situations. A revealing look at veterans, war, hyper-awareness, family, and the cost of carrying battlefield instincts into normal society.

recentItems.description:

--------
Ramon “Mundo” Mendoza sits down with VladTV for an uncensored account of his path from Boyle Heights altar boy to Mexican Mafia member known as “Machine Gun Mundo.” Born in East Los Angeles in 1949, Mendoza details childhood violence, early gang life, juvenile hall, San Quentin, Folsom, and the prison politics behind La Eme, Nuestra Familia, Norteños and Sureños. He discusses his first killing involving White Fence member Robert Lopez, his relationship with Joe “Pegleg” Morgan, street and prison hits he says totaled more than two dozen, and later cooperation with law enforcement after a Christian conversion.

Mendoza also addresses Kern County cases, witness protection, threats tied to organized crime, and Hollywood portrayals of the Mexican Mafia in *American Me*, including Edward James Olmos, Danny Trejo, and the controversy surrounding the film. A rare firsthand interview on gangs, prison power, informants, redemption, and consequences.
